Diagnostic Bilateral Mammogram with Tomosynthesis and Bilateral Ultrasound.

INDICATION: Left breast lump.

TECHNICAL FACTORS: Bilateral CC and MLO views were performed with tomosynthesis. Spot
compression views of the left breast were done. Bilateral global sonography was performed.

COMPARISON: None Available.

BREAST DENSITY: B Scattered Fibroglandular tissue is seen.

FINDINGS: A triangular skin marker has been placed on the upper central left breast, denoting the site
of reported palpable abnormality. There is an underlying 4 cm mass with spiculated and indistinct
margins.

Bilateral complete breast ultrasound was done. There is a hypoechoic mass with angular margins
measuring 4.1 cm at the 11 o'clock position, 1.6 cm from the nipple in the left breast, corresponding to
the mammographic finding that is better visualized on spot compression mammography. A hyperechoic
rim as of reported palpable abnormality. An enlarged axillary lymph node measuring 3.1 cm in the
left axilla. There is also an abnormal round lymph node measuring 1 cm in the left axilla as well.

CONCLUSION: Highly suspicious left breast mass at the 11 o'clock position with suspicious
corresponding axillary lymph nodes. Surgical consultation and tissue sampling are advised. The findings
and recommendations were discussed with Runas Rucker over the phone on August 21, 2025 at 1:00 p.m.

MRI LEFT AND BILATERAL (BILAT) W/O/W CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY: Highly suspicious imaging findings in the left breast at 6:00 4cm. Patient underwent ultrasound-guided biopsy in the left breast and 6/14 and 6/26/2025. Pathology is pending.

TECHNIQUE: Bilateral Breast MRI examination image standard protocol. Multi-plane sequences were performed in the axial and sagittal planes, including axial and two contrast with and without fat suppression. Axial post-contrast 3D and T1 subtraction images were obtained before and after gadolinium, allowing 3D image to be viewed planes, subtraction images and wash-out intensity projections with clearer disease kinetics.

COMPARISON: No prior breast MRI examinations are available for comparison. Correlation was made with prior relevant mammography and ultrasound from outside institution.

DENSITY: There is scattered fibroglandular tissue.

FINDINGS:

There is mild background parenchymal enhancement.

There is highly suspicious irregular enhancing and likely partially necrotic vascular mass in the upper medial/upper central left breast, measuring about 3.5 cm. There is associated biopsy marker clip. This was recently biopsied. Pathology is pending.

There is left axillary lymphadenopathy. The largest morphologically abnormal left axillary lymph node measures 1 cm and contains biopsy marker clip. Pathology is pending at this time.

There are no suspicious masses in the contralateral right breast.

There is no right axillary lymphadenopathy.

There is no internal mammary chain lymphadenopathy.

There is no abnormal chest wall or skin enhancement.

IMPRESSION:

1. Heterogeneous irregular enhancing mass resulting in the upper inner/upper central left breast. There is associated biopsy clip. Pathology is pending at this time. Patient will follow up with the breast surgeon and oncologist regarding the pathology results and further management.
